questions.question: Why does an elevated serum urate level alone not establish gout?
choices: Not everyone with hyperuricemia develops clinical crystal arthritis
It proves septic arthritis
It always identifies joint infection
It replaces joint examination
questions.explanation: Hyperuricemia is a risk factor but does not by itself diagnose clinical gout.

questions.question: Which situation requires urgent assessment rather than a routine gout refill?
choices: Hot swollen joint with fever after a recent skin infection
Stable known gout follow-up
A request for diet information
Improved walking after a prior flare
questions.explanation: Fever, infection risk, and acute monoarthritis raise concern for septic arthritis, which can coexist with gout.

questions.question: What is the purpose of acute gout-flare therapy?
choices: Control acute inflammation and pain using individualized safety considerations
Dissolve all crystals immediately
Replace long-term urate management
Treat every patient with the same medication
questions.explanation: Flare therapy treats current inflammation; medication choice depends on comorbidities, interactions, and diagnostic safety.

questions.question: What is the purpose of chronic urate-lowering therapy?
choices: Reduce urate burden over time and prevent future flares/crystal disease
Provide instant analgesia for every flare
Replace evaluation for infection
Treat asymptomatic hyperuricemia identically in all patients
questions.explanation: ULT lowers urate over time and is used for selected gout indications, not as an immediate analgesic.

questions.question: What does a treat-to-target ULT approach involve?
choices: Low-dose initiation with titration and serum-urate follow-up to reach a target
Keeping every patient on a fixed dose without monitoring
Stopping therapy after one normal day
Treating only with dietary advice
questions.explanation: ACR guidance emphasizes titration guided by serial serum urate, generally targeting less than 6 mg/dL for patients on ULT.

questions.question: Why may anti-inflammatory prophylaxis be used when initiating ULT?
choices: Starting or changing ULT can precipitate flares
ULT causes no changes in flare risk
It confirms septic arthritis
It replaces urate monitoring
questions.explanation: Urate shifts during ULT initiation can provoke flares, so prophylaxis and education are important when clinically appropriate.

questions.question: Which consideration is important before starting allopurinol in selected higher-risk populations?
choices: HLA-B*58:01 testing may be indicated to reduce severe hypersensitivity risk
Routine allergy testing is never relevant
CKD makes all ULT impossible
No medication reconciliation is needed
questions.explanation: Current guidance recommends HLA-B*58:01 testing before allopurinol in certain populations with higher allele prevalence and hypersensitivity risk.

questions.question: What should be reviewed in a patient with gout and CKD?
choices: Kidney-safe flare/ULT choices, drug interactions, monitoring, cardiovascular indications, and adherence
Only alcohol intake
Only joint color
No medications because of CKD
questions.explanation: CKD changes safety and dosing considerations but does not eliminate the need for individualized gout management.

questions.question: Which indication supports rheumatology referral in gout?
choices: Uncertain diagnosis, tophi, recurrent flares despite therapy, erosive disease, or complex CKD
A single controlled flare without questions
No symptoms and no treatment issues
Only a routine diet request
questions.explanation: Complex, refractory, tophaceous, or diagnostically uncertain gout can benefit from rheumatology collaboration.

questions.question: What is the FNP-level gout principle?
choices: Assume every red joint is gout
Exclude infection first, then separate flare care from goal-directed long-term urate management
Treat hyperuricemia and gout as identical
Use diet advice as the only plan
questions.explanation: Safe gout care prevents missed septic arthritis and builds individualized, monitored long-term urate control.
